command: php tools/external/escpos-php/capture.php character-tables && node tools/external/escpos-php/capture.js character-tables
notes: Exercises ESC t codepage switching, every byte of the first codepages. The example prints to a FilePrintConnector on php://stdout; the default capability profile names no paper, so the fixture is rendered on the 80 mm paper of the other fixtures. Reviewed as a PNG against what the example prints. Re-rendered on 2026-09-13, when the katakana codepage gained its glyphs from the second source of tools/generate.js and the glyphs that are wider than the face were fitted into their cell: the diff against the previous golden was reviewed by eye and holds only those two kinds of change, kana where the fallback box stood and a fitted glyph where a clipped left half stood. Re-rendered on 2026-09-14, when the Hebrew and the Thai of the code point set gained their glyphs from the third and the fourth source of tools/generate.js and three rules of the cell were added: a combining mark is centred in its cell by its ink instead of drawn from an origin it sits to the left of, a glyph whose ink lies outside its own advance is fitted by its ink instead of clipped at the edge of the cell, and a Unicode format character is an empty cell whether or not a source has a glyph for it. The diff against the previous golden was reviewed by eye row by row and holds only those changes: a letter where the fallback box stood, a mark where an empty cell stood, the two joiners of Windows-1256 turned from a sliver against the left wall of their cell into nothing, the two bidi marks of Windows-1255 and Windows-1256 turned from the fallback box into an empty cell, and the accents of ĥ ŉ Έ Ή Ί Ό Ύ Ώ, the tails of √ and ♫ and the nikhahit of the Thai ำ made whole where a column of them was clipped.
